Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Project: Rs 80,190 crore, 225 TMC a year, 147 TMC storage, lifts to 618 m
Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Sche: Rs 35,000 crore, 90 TMC a year, 67.5 TMC storage

norms.landcover: ESA WorldCover 2021 v200 at 320 m (CC BY 4.0)
norms.review: Norms, operating levels, the six trunk systems and the caveats follow a lift-irrigation engineering review of the model (24 October 2026); levels are recalled, not verified.

caveats: A planning sketch from a 200 m DEM and 320 m land cover; no survey, geology or hydrology behind any line.
Levels are approximate full-reservoir or drawdown levels recalled by the reviewer; the map's dam heights are ground at the structure, 5–55 m lower.
Water beyond the award: the Godavari draw needs a new interstate allocation; Krishna has no free water within the 299 TMC award, only flood years.
Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla suffered structural distress in 2023; their availability as intakes is not established.
Demand overlaps ayacut already promised to Kaleshwaram, Palamuru, Sitarama and Devadula; the true increment is smaller than shown.
Energy is the dominant recurring cost: water lifted 450–600 m costs Rs 30,000–40,000 an acre a year in power alone.
Routes may cross the Kawal and Amrabad tiger reserves and reserved forests; real alignments must avoid them.
Evaporation and seepage are a flat 12 % at the intake, not modelled site by site; villages inside pools are not counted, so resettlement is understated.
Groundwater, Mission Kakatiya tanks and treated Musi wastewater (about 25 TMC a year) are not counted as sources.
Tapped canals are assumed to spare 20 % of their design discharge; nothing here checks a head reservoir's dependable yield.

systems.name: S1 Pranahita – Adilabad plateau
systems.notes: Take Pranahita water above the confluence so the Godavari trough is never climbed out of; a 12 km tunnel crosses the Peddavagu–Kadam divide, a pressure main climbs the Utnur–Ichoda scarp; keep clear of the Kawal tiger reserve. Tummidihetti is an interstate barrage, proposed.

systems.name: S2 Kaleshwaram augmentation – Manjira and Zaheerabad–Vikarabad
systems.notes: Links I, II and IV as built, then a third-TMC augmentation of about 2.4 TMC a day for 100 days. The Manjira valley at Singur cuts the Siddipet plateau off from the 620–660 m Zaheerabad–Vikarabad plateau, so a 127 m re-lift is unavoidable; summit lift 584 m costs about Rs 39 crore of power per TMC. Medigadda's condition after 2023 must be verified; Yellampalli is the fallback intake.

systems.name: S3 Sammakka Sagar – Devadula – Jangaon ridge to Nalgonda
systems.notes: Sammakka Sagar sits below the Indravati confluence and has the most reliable surplus. Devadula's pressure mains would have to become a canal or tunnel at 377 cumecs. Dharmasagar commands Warangal, Mahabubabad, Mulugu and Jayashankar by gravity; a Jangaon pool feeds a ridge canal along the Aler–Motkur–Ramannapet watershed to Chityal and Nalgonda, with a branch to Suryapet, putting Godavari water into Krishna-basin districts so the Krishna share stays free.

systems.name: S4 Sitarama – Palvancha – Yellandu
systems.notes: Overlaps the Sitarama lift scheme under construction for the same districts: count only the increment. Yellandu commands Khammam, Wyra and Sathupalli by gravity; Palvancha the Kothagudem lowland.

systems.name: S5 Palamuru–Rangareddy extension – Kulkacherla summit and Dindi
systems.notes: Srisailam intake near its minimum drawdown (~245 m). Palamuru pools as designed, levels approximate. A new 70 m stage reaches Kulkacherla, the summit of the Krishna–Godavari divide, commanding Shadnagar, Kothur, Maheshwaram, Chevella and southern Vikarabad. Dindi is fed by gravity from Yedula. Entirely beyond the 299 TMC award: Krishna flood water only.

systems.name: S6 Jurala – Bhima – Nettempadu
systems.notes: Bhima and Nettempadu pools as existing, levels approximate. A new 125 m stage to Kosgi commands Narayanpet and Kodangal. Krishna flood water only.
